prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System: underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering; initialization/protected-manual/automatic/fallback/cutout. Degraded operation requires separation/trusted communications; automatic restoration requires stable communications, verified routes/positions, recorded handback, Line Traffic Controller authorization.
Metro Operations Control System (Lantern), nonvital, sends Crew Login Token Bundle; requires Test Train Clearance Memo from Revenue Train Operator before protected-territory non-revenue security exceptions. Operator controls movement/doors, reads back restrictions; no cybersecurity administration during passenger service. Voice Dispatch Console authorizes restricted-manual, never substitutes safety validation/locking.
North District Zone Controller (Marble)/South District Zone Controller (Orchid) validate boundaries/overlaps; North validates Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; South inhibits automatic routes under manual occupancy. East Junction Interlocking (Falcon)/West Junction Interlocking prove routes; East sends Axle Counter Reset Request; West sends Route Release Exception List to controller. Signal Maintenance Engineer verifies manual routes; controller/engineer concur occupancy-changing resets. Maple unidentified; records clearance.
Platform Screen Door Controller produces Platform Door Status Snapshot; doors constrain departure. Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel) validates authority, enforces braking, produces Brake Curve Checksum Log. Dual Channel Odometer supplies distance/speed/confidence. Train Radio Modem sends Radio Handover Audit File; Cyber Security Officer investigates continuity/completeness.
Officer continuously monitors Safety Data Communication Network, Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron), and Lantern; correlates authentication/session/message/configuration/timing anomalies without changing safety paths; classifies availability alerts by impact/territory/authority-risk; notifies controller of automatic/communications restrictions.
Cryptographic Key Management Appliance controls certificates, produces Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack; issuance requires approved identity/baseline/domain/service authorization; renew before expiry; revoke compromised/retired/unreconciled devices. Falcon rejects invalid signatures/expired certificates/out-of-window sequences. Maintenance Diagnostic Server cannot bypass trust. Appliance administration requires named accounts/MFA/separated duties/approved changes; officer approves engineer’s security-sensitive access. Audit evidence: synchronized events/approvals/certificate-actions/configurations/alarm-acknowledgements/operator-instructions.
Service Timetable Server supplies approved/controller-verified context; Passenger Information Gateway receives reconciliation.

New part:
S218: Audit records shall be protected from local alteration by the component that generates them and shall be retained for the period defined by Greenvale Metro governance.
S219: The Service Timetable Server and Passenger Information Gateway shall be monitored for compromise because incorrect operational context can influence control room decisions even when safety commands remain valid.
S220: The Voice Dispatch Console shall be included in security incident procedures when a cyber event changes the normal method for issuing operational instructions.
S221: The Platform Screen Door Controller shall accept only authenticated interfaces approved for passenger service coordination and maintenance testing.
S222: The Dual Channel Odometer and Atlas Onboard Controller shall report security-relevant diagnostic conditions in a manner that supports investigation without exposing cryptographic material.
S223: Security responsibilities shall be reviewed after major timetable changes, radio coverage modifications, control center upgrades, or any incident that questions the integrity of safety-related communications.
S224: Commissioning shall begin only after the installed equipment baseline for the Atlas Onboard Controller, Dual Channel Odometer, Train Radio Modem, and wayside control equipment has been configuration checked against the approved release record.
S225: The test-train phase shall use non-passenger movements to prove train localization, movement authority processing, braking response, radio continuity, and operator displays under controlled operating conditions.
S226: Each test train shall be crewed by a Revenue Train Operator qualified for commissioning duties and supported by a Line Traffic Controller with authority to stop the trial when observed conditions depart from the approved script.
S227: Initial movements shall be conducted at restricted commissioning speeds and shall progress to representative service speeds only after the Atlas Onboard Controller and North District Zone Controller demonstrate stable supervision.
S228: The South District Zone Controller shall be commissioned under the same test regime so that boundary behavior is verified before whole-line operation is attempted.
S229: East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking shall remain under enhanced monitoring during migration because route setting, point detection, and authority release behavior are critical to mixed-mode operation.
S230: The staged migration from legacy signalling shall divide the railway into controlled areas that can be commissioned, operated, and, if necessary, returned to legacy control without affecting uncommissioned areas.
S231: Cutover planning shall define the exact control boundaries, permissible train movements, staffing levels, and rollback conditions for each migration stage.
S232: Before any cutover stage, the Safety Data Communication Network and Wayside Radio Access Network shall be verified for coverage, latency, redundancy, and alarm presentation at the control center.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
